title: Retrieval-Augmented Hypergraph for Multimodal Social Media Popularity Prediction

problem.claim: Predicting the popularity of multimodal user-generated content supports applications including advertising and recommendation.

gap.claim: Existing methods use limited context from individual items and generally do not exploit useful knowledge from related user-generated content.

contributions.claim: RAGTrans is an aspect-aware retrieval-augmented multimodal hypergraph transformer that retrieves knowledge from a multimodal memory bank and aggregates neighborhood knowledge to enrich content representations.

The method constructs a knowledge-enhanced hypergraph from aspect-relevant multimedia instances and uses a bootstrapping hypergraph transformer to propagate information across multimodal nodes and edges.
A user-aware attention-based fusion module combines enriched content representations for popularity prediction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the bootstrapping hypergraph transformer as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world social media datasets are reported to show that RAGTrans outperforms state-of-the-art popularity prediction models across settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal content popularity prediction is presented as important for practical applications.
Prior approaches are characterized as underusing contextual knowledge from related content.
RAGTrans retrieves aspect-relevant multimedia instances and builds a knowledge-enhanced multimodal hypergraph.
A bootstrapping transformer propagates information across hypergraph nodes and edges to strengthen multimodal representations.
User-aware fusion supports popularity prediction, with reported gains over existing models in experiments.

source_observation.claim: The approach combines retrieval of related multimodal instances with hypergraph-based neighborhood aggregation.

interpretation.claim: Prediction may benefit when relevant external context is organized into a structure that supports cross-instance information sharing.

application.claim: For related-content prediction tasks, consider retrieving context by task-relevant aspects and aggregating it across multimodal relationships.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported social media datasets and settings.

unknowns: Dataset names, sizes, and preprocessing are unspecified.
